clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Herbalism directs budding herbalists to local profession trainers across Azeroth, such as Faruza in Brill, to master the craft of Incense Candles. These aromatic creations provide vital restorative aid to spellcasters resting in wilderness camps.

While herbalism is commonly seen as the groundwork for alchemy, practical field survival relies just as heavily on gathered roots and blossoms. Experienced travelers point aspiring foragers toward regional master herbalists to learn how to prepare Incense Candles. In the Tirisfal Glades, Eleanor Shackleton directs promising foragers to visit Faruza in Brill once they demonstrate fundamental skill.

Life on the road takes a heavy mental toll on spellcasters and spiritualists. Incense Candles release restorative fragrances meant to lift spirits and soothe weary minds. By infusing dried plants into candles, gatherers provide crucial aid to the healers and mages whose magical reserves falter during extended travel.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Looks to me like you've gained some skill in herbalism. Picking flowers isn't just for dilly-dallying, you know. It can be useful... And profitable.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft an Incense Candle for your camp. High spirits are a key component to keeping healers and spellcasters in the fight, and an Incense Candle can provide a boost that magic users will surely appreciate.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Incense Candle. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
